fixer.title: sessions: stop polling the Agent Host session list when a listing fails to apply

introducer.title: sessions: recover empty Agent Host session list after a failed initial refresh

cases.mechanism: A deterministic exception while applying an already-returned session catalog entered the network-failure retry path after the backoff had been reset, repeatedly fetching and deserializing the complete remote catalog once per second.
cases.symptom: Opening/reconnecting an affected Agent Host could continuously transfer and deserialize the full session list at 1 Hz, consuming remote connection bandwidth and making an SSH-backed sessions window unresponsive.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added didList flag distinguishes a rejected listSessions boundary from failure after a listing was returned. At RIGHT line 7998, post-list failures are logged and returned without arming the retry timer, while genuine connection/auth listing failures retain the exponential-backoff retry. Per-row registration conflicts are also isolated so remaining rows can reconcile.
cases.evidence: Before this diff, one catch covered both the listSessions RPC and all synchronous reconciliation. A successful RPC reset _sessionRefreshRetryDelay to the 1s minimum at base line 7902; if createAdapter/registerBackendSession or a later reconciliation hook then threw, that same catch called _scheduleSessionRefreshRetry. The next successful full-list RPC reset the delay again before the deterministic apply failure, producing a full list request every second. The added test advances 10 seconds and requires exactly one list call for a deterministic apply failure, directly exercising the old repeated-request path.
